about: Permanent chat trajectory test plan, written by the user. Tier 1 dialogues run VERBATIM — on the device (type each user turn into Jeeves chat) or headlessly via JeevesTests/TrajectoryTests. Tier 2 escalations are generated per run by scenario-eval.py against briefs/chat-trajectories.md; Tier 3 injects failures. After any run: pull the store, run trajectory-audit.py (deterministic) and the story-vs-state judges. A scenario passes only when BOTH agree.

fields.turns: The scenario in the user's own words. Never paraphrase these — they are the specification.
fields.answers: Replies fed ONLY after every scripted turn is done and the assistant is still asking something, in order. Real users answer; a one-way script made the app's (correct) request for a missing checkout date look like a failure to act. Answers never interleave with the script — injecting them mid-scenario once answered 'a hotel for the Singapore stay?' with 'two nights at Wayanad' and derailed the run.
fields.expect: What a correct build must leave behind.

sequencing: Scenarios share one store and run in order. 2, 3 and 11 act on the event 1 created; 7, 8, 9 and 10 build on and then move the itinerary 5 started; 12 lists whatever exists by then; 13 is a fresh chain; 14 modifies what is left. Running one alone tests far less than running the sequence. The numbering is the user's and skips 6.

turns: Add dinner with Arvind tomorrow at 8 pm
It's at Toit, Indiranagar
tier1.expect: ONE event, correct day, 20:00 start with a sensible end, venue set via edit (not a second event). If no end time was given the receipt SAYS the end was assumed. Planner shows the commute leg for it.

turns: I'm at the dinner, it's running long — extend it by an hour
tier1.expect: The SAME event's end moves +60 minutes — via extend_by_minutes, never a computed clock time, and never a shrink. No duplicate. The receipt quotes the old and the new range. If the event is today a replan of the remainder is OFFERED, not silently skipped, and elapsed blocks before it are not marked missed.

turns: Stuck in traffic on the way to the dinner, push it 30 minutes
tier1.expect: Start AND end move +30 together (shift_by_minutes — duration preserved, not stretched). Any replan uses resume_at = the new start and marks blocks the delay swallowed via missed_blocks — ELAPSED IS NOT DONE.

turns: Set up a 4 day trip to Colombo starting the 20th of next month
Outbound flight UL 174 departs BLR 09:45, return UL 173 departs Colombo 20:30 on the last day, lands BLR 22:00
answers: Leaving from home in Indiranagar, Bengaluru airport both ways
tier1.expect: One trip, 4 days, end date AFTER start. Exactly TWO flight journeys — no duplicate from restating a leg: outbound origin-clock IST, return origin-clock Asia/Colombo, zones stamped on BOTH legs. Leave-by chains on the right days; two nudges; no second trip from the second turn.

turns: I'm in Singapore till the 10th of next month, flying back SQ 510 departing 19:40 SGT, landing BLR 21:10
Next morning I drive to Mysore, staying at Radisson hotel Mysore for 2 days, then checkout
tier1.expect: TWO trips sharing the handover day, never merged — the Mysore itinerary must NOT be absorbed into the Singapore trip. Radisson Blu Mysore stay of exactly 2 nights, one measured drive from home to Mysore, and the return flight stamped Asia/Singapore. One journey per leg. The handover day shows both trips' cards.

turns: Add one more day to the Mysore trip
Actually cut the last day, end it a day earlier
tier1.expect: update_trip/update_stay both times — no new trip, no duplicate, and the SHRINK must actually happen (a reply saying it went back with no tool call behind it is a fabrication). EVERY turn gets a reply. Growth sweeps plans on the new day; shrink says the freed day goes back to the planner. Receipts quote the old AND the new ranges.

turns: From Mysore I drive to Wayanad and stay at CGH Earth Wayanad
Checkout from Wayanad three days later and drive back home, I want to reach home by 6 pm
answers: Checkout the morning of the third day, driving home to Indiranagar
tier1.expect: CGH Earth Wayanad stay of three nights on the SAME trip as Mysore, a measured Radisson → CGH Earth drive transition, and a return drive whose leave-by works BACKWARDS from arriving home at 18:00 on the DESTINATION clock. Exactly one journey per leg — never a second copy under another trip. The trip window grows to cover the Wayanad days.

turns: Postpone the Wayanad checkout by 2 days — make it a 5 day stay
tier1.expect: The SAME CGH Earth stay extends from 3 nights to 5 — update_stay, never a second stay. The trip window grows with it, the drive home moves to the new checkout day and is RE-MEASURED for that day, its leave-by still works back from 18:00, and its old nudge is cancelled and re-armed. The receipt quotes the old range and the new one.

turns: Push the whole Mysore trip back by 7 days — everything moves a week later
answers: Yes, the stays and the drives too
tier1.expect: The trip, BOTH stays and EVERY journey shift exactly 7 days — nothing left behind on the old dates and nothing duplicated. Critically the FREED days stop being travel days: the planner takes them back and they render as normal days, not travel mode. Nudges for the old dates are cancelled and re-armed on the new ones. The receipt names the old window and the new one.

turns: Postpone my dinner with Arvind by a day
Actually prepone it — bring it forward two days
tier1.expect: Plain 'postpone' and 'prepone' are understood without a clarifying question: the SAME event moves +1 day, then −2 days from there, keeping its time of day and duration. No duplicate event, no new event. Each receipt quotes the day it moved from and to.

turns: Show me all my upcoming events
Now show my upcoming journeys
tier1.expect: BOTH answers are read from stored data, never from the conversation. Every event and every journey that exists is listed with its date — and a journey answer must come from the journeys themselves, not from calendar events that happen to look like travel. If a collection is empty it says so plainly. Nothing is invented, and nothing real is omitted.

turns: Plan this: I drive to Wayanad on Friday and stay at CGH Earth Wayanad
I check out from CGH Earth on Monday morning and drive to Western Valley Resort near Ooty, staying there the next two days, then home before 6 pm
Checkout at all the hotels is before 11:30 am, check-in starts after 2 pm, and breakfast is served 7:30 to 10:30 am — work the drives around that
answers: This coming Friday, driving from home in Indiranagar
Yes, two nights at Western Valley, home on the third day
tier1.expect: Day-of-week arithmetic right: Friday check-in, Monday checkout = THREE nights at CGH Earth. A measured Wayanad → Western Valley drive that LEAVES after breakfast and before the 11:30 checkout and ARRIVES after the 14:00 check-in — and if it cannot satisfy both, says so rather than silently picking one. Two nights at Western Valley, then a return drive working back from 18:00 at home. One stay per hotel, one journey per leg, despite three turns of constraints.

turns: Move the Radisson stay to start a day later
Delete the stay at Western Valley
Delete all trips on the 15th
Extend whatever event I have on the 12th by two hours
tier1.expect: Each modification lands via the matching key the user chose — hotel name, date, location — with a preview/confirm on the destructive ones, receipts naming exactly what changed, and zero duplicates created by any of the four turns.

tier2.generate: OPENAI_API_KEY=... python3 tools/scenario-eval.py generate tools/briefs/chat-trajectories.md <outdir> — regenerates escalations each run; never hand-pick them.
axes: clock seams: +5:45/+6:00 offsets, red-eyes crossing midnight, deadline in destination clock
order of operations: stay before trip, calendar sync after chat built the same trip, flight before its trip
corrections + consent: 'actually make that Tuesday', bare 'Sure', correction AFTER confirmation, exact repeat of a request (idempotency)
cross-entity deletion: event vs trip vs stay in one sentence ('clear my September')
failure injection: measure timeout then manual estimate then re-measure; planner API down (fallback must respect the trip); a dropped turn (apology must surface)
interleaving: a gym replan interrupts trip planning, then 'anyway, back to the trip'
long horizon: build 3 weeks out, resync calendar twice, modify once, audit must stay clean
policy constraints: checkout/check-in windows and meal times that make a leg infeasible — the refusal must be explicit

tier3.note: Chaos runs — execute a Tier 1 dialogue while: airplane mode toggled mid-conversation, app backgrounded mid-tool-call, watch delivering a workout summary simultaneously. Pass = graceful receipts or honest apologies; FAIL = silence, duplicates, or claimed actions that didn't happen.

gaps.note: Known coverage gaps — recorded so their absence is deliberate, not forgotten.
missing: the planner itself: plan quality and travel-day stand-down have no dialogue of their own
fitness/Watch: no dialogue touches workouts (those surface via the anomaly digest)
refusal path: no dialogue declines a destructive action after seeing its preview
everyday data questions (longest walk, page in a book, best lift) are untested
idempotent replay: running a dialogue twice must not double anything
relaunch survival: nothing checks state after the app restarts

verification: Every run: python3 tools/diagnose.py <workdir> --pull  (store-audit + trajectory-audit deterministic layer), then tools/trajectory-judge.py on the artifact (Claude + GPT, strictest verdict wins, Fable 5 breaks ties). Pass requires: zero duplicate trips/stays/journeys, every assistant number traceable to a tool result, every claimed action present in the store, no unanswered turns. Run-to-run variance is large — six runs on near-identical code produced 25/21/14/11/23/11 tool calls — so a single run is a smoke test, not a verdict: repeat each dialogue 3-5 times, require the deterministic invariants at 100%, and report judged scores as a mean with its spread.
